acceptance_criteria.description: The embedded helper remains live across multiple inspect/control frames and closes only on explicit release, controller EOF, or fatal failure.
Target I/O cannot spoof helper protocol; bounded target output remains observable through the existing onOutput seam without exposing control frames.

Full createWindowsProcessAdapter native spawn/inspect/terminate/release returns terminated or already-exited (never retryable for the healthy disposable child), proves target absence and helper exit, and affects no unrelated process.
Focused suite, build, and bounded Windows native proof pass; raw-PID fallback remains unavailable/non-release-grade and docs match actual lifecycle behavior.

closed_decisions: Root-observed failure is authoritative: full createWindowsProcessAdapter spawn -> custody.inspect -> custody.terminate failed with 'Windows Job handle is unavailable' although the lower-level proof passed.

The target must not share the helper control stdin/stdout. Give the target a non-control stdin and route target stdout/stderr through a separate inherited handle or explicit bounded frames that cannot be parsed as control responses; frame-like target output must never satisfy a pending control request.

The helper must read control bytes from the actual standard-input stream and remain alive until explicit release, controller EOF, or fatal bounded protocol/native failure. Controller EOF must close the Job and kill remaining members.
Control requests must enqueue one paired resolver/rejector before writing, remove both together, reject all on helper loss, and enforce finite frame/output/pending/time bounds.

Termination convergence must be based on the target process held in the Job, not the helper ChildProcess exit. A successful Job termination must wait boundedly for the held target handle to signal; subsequent native inspect returns absence, while helper remains available until release.

The full tracked-adapter Windows native proof must spawn only a disposable child, prove identity-bound inspect, terminate without retryable state, prove target absence, release, and prove helper exit. Preserve no-supported-raw-PID fallback and Linux behavior.

focused: pnpm vitest run tests/unit/windows-job-object.test.ts tests/unit/windows-custody.test.ts tests/unit/windows-process.test.ts tests/unit/process-custody.test.ts tests/platform/ownership-proof.test.ts tests/platform/background-proof.test.ts tests/release/release-safety.test.ts
natural: On Windows, run a bounded full createWindowsProcessAdapter spawn/inspect/terminate/release proof using only a disposable child and verify target absence plus helper exit.

forbidden_changes: Do not edit session manager, provider/dialog behavior, dependencies/lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, git, Jira, or pull requests.

Do not treat helper exit as target exit, share target stdin with the control channel, parse target bytes as control frames, kill/revalidate by raw PID, weaken the suspended assignment barrier, or target any unrelated process in proof.
objective: Repair the Windows Job bridge so the full tracked adapter retains live handle-bound custody through inspect, termination, and release, with target I/O isolated from the control protocol.
